answer_text: The v2.5 settlement release slipped about two weeks because a settlement idempotency bug (LED-412) was found in staging: the settlement path could post a charge twice on retry. The team deliberately held the release (PAY-501 was blocked-by LED-412) until the fix was merged and verified in staging (commit a9), then cut the release two weeks past the original target.

Release deliberately held until the fix was verified

answer_text: The June 3 duplicate charges resulted from a retry storm hitting an unprotected settlement path. Risk Engine scoring timeouts under load caused the payment path to retry (RISK-220 / commit a3). Those retries landed on a settlement hot path whose idempotency guard had recently been disabled for performance (commit a1); with the guard off, retried settlements were no longer deduplicated and charges posted twice. It was resolved by reverting that change to re-enable the check (PAY-540 / commit a15).
root_causes: Risk Engine timeouts caused the payment path to retry (RISK-220 / a3)
Idempotency guard disabled on the settlement hot path (commit a1)
With the guard off, retries were no longer deduplicated, causing duplicate charges

Explains the mechanism: with the guard removed, retried charges were no longer deduplicated
Identifies the fix: revert / re-enable the guard (PAY-540 / a15)

answer_text: FinFlow chose asynchronous settlement over synchronous to increase throughput and reduce payment latency: synchronous writes coupled payment latency to ledger-write latency and capped throughput. The accepted tradeoff is an eventual-consistency window between charge and ledger entry, plus a double-posting risk on retry. That risk was mitigated by making settlement carry idempotency keys (ADR-004), which was treated as a hard requirement of the async design.
root_causes: Async chosen for throughput / lower payment latency
Alternative considered was synchronous settlement
Tradeoff: an eventual-consistency window
Double-posting risk mitigated by idempotency keys (ADR-004)

answer_text: The June 9 duplicate notifications happened because the notification event bus is at-least-once (ADR-003), so the consumer must deduplicate redeliveries — but a recent consumer refactor (commit a4) had dropped the dedup step. With dedup gone, every redelivery was sent as a duplicate. It was fixed by re-adding event-id deduplication to the consumer (NOT-320 / commit a5).
root_causes: The event bus is at-least-once, requiring consumer dedup (ADR-003)
A recent refactor dropped the dedup step (commit a4)
Redeliveries were no longer collapsed, causing duplicate notifications

Identifies that dedup was dropped in a recent refactor (commit a4)
Explains the mechanism: at-least-once plus no dedup yields duplicates
Identifies the fix: re-add dedup (NOT-320 / a5)
